primary.title: On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules
primary.author: Niels Bohr
primary.rationale: This is Bohr's seminal paper outlining his model of the atom, a foundational text in quantum mechanics. It is highly likely to be available in digital archives.

primary.title: Atomic Physics and Human Knowledge
primary.author: Niels Bohr
primary.rationale: A collection of essays and lectures by Bohr, discussing the philosophical implications of quantum mechanics and his concept of complementarity. Such collections are often digitized.

primary.title: The Theory of Spectra and the Constitution of Atoms
primary.author: Niels Bohr
primary.rationale: This is the text of Bohr's Nobel Prize lecture, a significant primary source detailing his contributions to atomic theory. Nobel lectures are often preserved and digitized.

secondary.title: Niels Bohr's Philosophy of Quantum Physics
secondary.author: Jørgen Kalckar
secondary.rationale: This book delves into Bohr's philosophical contributions, particularly his concept of complementarity, offering scholarly analysis of his work.

secondary.title: Niels Bohr: His Life and Work as Seen by His Friends and Colleagues
secondary.author: S. Rozental
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, this is a highly regarded collection of essays by those who knew Bohr, providing invaluable biographical and scientific context. It's a standard reference.

secondary.title: The Bohr-Einstein Dialogues
secondary.author: Don Howard
secondary.rationale: This article likely analyzes the famous debates between Bohr and Einstein on the foundations of quantum mechanics, a crucial aspect of Bohr's scientific legacy.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are chosen based on their foundational importance and likelihood of being digitized. Secondary sources focus on scholarly analysis of Bohr's work and philosophy, with a preference for academic books and articles.
